1.0: RESOLVED: The United States Supreme Court ruled in Brown v. Board of Education (1954) that racial segregation in public schools was unconstitutional.
1.1: DOCUMENT: Brown v. Board of Education, 347 U.S. 483 (1954) - unanimous Supreme Court decision
1.2: ASSERTS: The ruling held that state-mandated racial segregation in public schools violated the Equal Protection Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment
1.3: ASSERTS: Chief Justice Earl Warren wrote for a unanimous Court that 'separate educational facilities are inherently unequal'
1.4: ASSERTS: The decision explicitly overruled the 'separate but equal' doctrine established in Plessy v. Ferguson (1896) as applied to public education
1.5: RESOLVED: This is settled historical and legal fact with an unambiguous holding
1.6: DOCUMENT: Brown v. Board of Education (Brown II), 349 U.S. 294 (1955) - subsequent remedial decision addressing implementation
1.7: ASSERTS: Brown I (1954) made an unqualified constitutional holding that racial segregation in public schools violates Equal Protection - without permitting continued segregation
1.8: ASSERTS: Brown II (1955) addressed remedy and timeline for implementation, not the constitutional principle itself
1.9: ASSERTS: The phrase 'all deliberate speed' appeared only in Brown II regarding implementation timing, not in the constitutional holding
1.10: REJECTS: Claim that Brown v. Board of Education permitted segregation to continue as long as schools worked toward desegregation - this misstates the constitutional holding
1.11: ASSERTS: Brown II's 'all deliberate speed' framework addressed practical implementation questions, not whether segregation was constitutional
1.12: ASSERTS: The ambiguous 'all deliberate speed' language in Brown II enabled massive resistance and delayed actual integration for years in practice
1.13: ASSERTS: Brown II did not reverse, qualify, or permit exceptions to Brown I's constitutional holding - segregation remained unconstitutional throughout the implementation period
